components.cost_effect: Two exact F calls and two exact prox solves per iteration.
components.goal: Control the smoothness residual while telescoping the Bregman potential.
components.key_estimate: For every u∈Z, gamma<F(w),w-u>≤V(u,z)-V(u,z+) when gamma L≤alpha/sqrt(2); see the complete argument in thm.P068.gap_bound.
components.name: Common-base predictor-corrector
components.operation: First prox uses F(z), second uses F(w), both based at z.
components.requires: Z nonempty convex compact in finite-dimensional E; arbitrary norm and its dual; F monotone and ||F(z)-F(v)||*≤L||z-v|| for all z,v∈Z, L>0; differentiable omega with V(u,z)≥alpha||u-z||²/2, alpha>0; exact F and exact global prox minimizers. Source uses continuously differentiable omega; the separate local Theorem argument uses only differentiability and this Bregman inequality.
transfer_checks: Recompute alpha,L and Theta under a new geometry.
Reestablish the one-step inequality for stochastic Oracles, inexact prox solves or altered feasible sets.

limitations.statement: The rate concerns the predictor average, not the final corrected iterate or an unrestricted Oracle lower bound.

performance_links.scope_note: The assigned Theorem covers the selected fixed gamma and the same full-prefix predictor average.

variants.cost: Exactly two F evaluations and two exact prox minimization calls per step in the stated implementation: 2T of each, plus one initial omega minimization. Computing gradients of omega, running sums and all arithmetic/inner work of prox solves are additional resources, not free F calls. No universal arithmetic cost for a prox solve is asserted.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF pp.4–11 / printed pp.232–239; (3.2), Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2, (4.2). The fixed two-step rule does not adopt the adaptive inner stopping of (3.4) or Hölder tuning of (4.3).
variants.name: Fixed two-step, full-prefix predictor average
variants.output: wbar_T=(1/T)sum_{t=1}^T w_t∈Z. In product domains return its two coordinate averages.
public_inputs: Z, norm/dual norm, omega and exact prox solver
Known valid alpha>0 and L>0; integer T≥1
variants.query_and_update: For t=1,...,T: query a_t=F(z_{t-1}); w_t=argmin_{u∈Z}{gamma<a_t,u>+V(u,z_{t-1})}; query b_t=F(w_t); z_t=argmin_{u∈Z}{gamma<b_t,u>+V(u,z_{t-1})}. Both prox solves have base z_{t-1}.
variants.requirements: Z nonempty convex compact in finite-dimensional E; arbitrary norm and its dual; F monotone and ||F(z)-F(v)||*≤L||z-v|| for all z,v∈Z, L>0; differentiable omega with V(u,z)≥alpha||u-z||²/2, alpha>0; exact F and exact global prox minimizers. Source uses continuously differentiable omega; the separate local Theorem argument uses only differentiability and this Bregman inequality.
variants.state_and_initialization: Compute z0∈argmin_Z omega separately. Set gamma=alpha/(sqrt(2)L); V(u,z)=omega(u)-omega(z)-<grad omega(z),u-z>. Keep current z and a running sum of predictors.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Run exactly T steps with constant gamma; no extra fixed-point termination query is required. Any fixed 0<gamma≤alpha/(sqrt(2)L) is covered by the assigned Theorem. If an accuracy target epsilon>0 and a public upper bound B≥Theta(z0) are supplied, T≥max(1,ceil(B/(gamma epsilon))) suffices.
